candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — shared blood glucose meter reprocessing
candidate.client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
candidate.educational_objective: When a blood glucose meter must be shared, use a device intended for professional multi-patient use and clean and disinfect it after every client according to manufacturer instructions; do not share a meter lacking validated reprocessing instructions.

options.A: Use a meter designed for professional multi-patient use and clean and disinfect it after every client according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
options.B: Wipe the meter once at the end of the shift because a new lancet is used for each client.
options.C: Share any over-the-counter home glucose meter as long as visible blood is wiped away between clients.
options.D: Continue sharing the meter even if the manufacturer provides no validated cleaning and disinfection instructions.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC recommends assigning blood glucose meters to individual patients whenever possible. If a meter must be shared in a health care or congregate setting, it should be a device designed for professional use and must be cleaned and disinfected after every use according to the manufacturer’s instructions. If the manufacturer does not specify how the device should be cleaned and disinfected, the meter should not be shared. B is insufficient because contamination can occur with each use. C is incorrect because over-the-counter home meters are not automatically suitable for professional multi-patient use. D directly contradicts CDC guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Shared glucose meters require validated cleaning and disinfection after every patient use and should be designed for professional multi-patient use; meters without manufacturer reprocessing instructions should not be shared.
candidate.source_document_title: Considerations for Blood Glucose Monitoring and Insulin Administration
